concepts.name: Legal Architecture of the Paris Agreement: Binding vs. Non-Binding Elements
key_dimensions: Which provisions are legally binding (e.g., obligation to submit NDCs) vs. non-binding (e.g., the NDC targets themselves)
Contrast with Kyoto Protocol's top-down binding emission targets
The 'shall' vs. 'should' distinction in treaty language and its implications
Why this hybrid structure was a deliberate political compromise — UPSC trap: confusing 'agreement is binding' with 'targets are binding'

concepts.name: The 1.5°C vs. 2°C Temperature Targets: Origins, Differences, and Scientific Basis
key_dimensions: Article 2(1)(a): 'well below 2°C' AND 'pursue efforts to limit to 1.5°C' — both targets coexist
IPCC Special Report on 1.5°C (SR1.5, 2018): key findings on differential impacts between 1.5°C and 2°C
Pre-industrial baseline reference point and how it is measured
UPSC trap: assuming the Paris Agreement sets only a 1.5°C target; the 2°C target is primary with 1.5°C as aspirational

concepts.name: Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs): Structure, Submission, and Progression Principle
key_dimensions: Article 4: each Party must prepare, communicate, and maintain successive NDCs
The 'progression principle' — each new NDC must represent an advance on the previous one (ratchet mechanism)
Five-year NDC cycle: submission timeline and the 2020, 2025, 2030 milestones
UPSC trap: NDCs are nationally determined — there is NO international body that approves or rejects them

concepts.name: India's NDC Commitments: Original (2015), Updated (2022), and Long-Term Strategy
key_dimensions: Original 3 targets: 33–35% emissions intensity reduction by 2030 (vs. 2005), 40% non-fossil electricity capacity, 2.5–3 billion tonnes CO2 equivalent carbon sink
Updated 2022 NDC: intensity target raised to 45%, non-fossil capacity raised to 50% by 2030
India's Long-Term Low Emission Development Strategy (LT-LEDS) submitted at COP27
UPSC trap: India has NOT committed to an absolute emissions reduction target — only emissions intensity (GDP-linked) reduction

concepts.name: Common but Differentiated Responsibilities and Respective Capabilities (CBDR-RC) in Paris Agreement
key_dimensions: How Paris Agreement reformulates CBDR-RC compared to UNFCCC and Kyoto Protocol — no longer Annex I/Non-Annex I binary
Phrase 'in the light of different national circumstances' added — a significant dilution of historical responsibility
Developed vs. developing country obligations: finance, technology transfer, capacity building
UPSC trap: Paris Agreement does NOT use the Annex I/Annex II/Non-Annex I classification of the original UNFCCC

concepts.name: Global Stocktake (GST): Mechanism, Frequency, and First Outcomes
key_dimensions: Article 14: collective assessment of progress toward Paris Agreement goals every 5 years
First GST completed at COP28 (Dubai, 2023) — key findings: current NDCs insufficient for 1.5°C
GST informs but does NOT mandate revision of NDCs — soft pressure mechanism
UPSC trap: GST is a collective assessment, NOT an assessment of individual country performance

concepts.name: Loss and Damage: Article 8 and the Santiago Network to the COP28 Fund
key_dimensions: Article 8 of Paris Agreement: acknowledges importance of averting, minimizing, and addressing loss and damage
Warsaw International Mechanism (WIM) for Loss and Damage — predates Paris Agreement
COP27 (Sharm el-Sheikh) breakthrough: agreement to establish a dedicated Loss and Damage fund
COP28: operationalization of the fund — hosted by World Bank initially; UPSC trap: Article 8 explicitly states it does NOT involve liability or compensation

concepts.name: Climate Finance: $100 Billion Goal, New Collective Quantified Goal (NCQG), and Article 9
key_dimensions: Article 9: developed countries SHALL provide financial resources to developing countries — one of the few binding finance obligations
$100 billion/year by 2020 goal — first promised in Copenhagen Accord 2009, not met on time
New Collective Quantified Goal (NCQG): to be set by 2025, replacing the $100 billion floor — COP29 (Baku) mandate
UPSC trap: the $100 billion figure is NOT in the Paris Agreement text itself — it is in the accompanying COP Decision

concepts.name: Net Zero Emissions: Concept, Article 4.1, and National Net Zero Targets
key_dimensions: Article 4.1: 'achieve a balance between anthropogenic emissions by sources and removals by sinks' — this is the treaty's net zero formulation
Difference between 'carbon neutrality,' 'net zero,' and 'climate neutrality'
India's net zero target: 2070 (announced at COP26, Glasgow) — not yet in India's official NDC
UPSC trap: the term 'net zero' does NOT appear in the Paris Agreement text; Article 4.1 uses 'balance' language

concepts.name: Carbon Markets under Article 6: Cooperative Approaches and the Rulebook
key_dimensions: Article 6.2: bilateral cooperative approaches (country-to-country trading) using Internationally Transferred Mitigation Outcomes (ITMOs)
Article 6.4: new centralized UN-supervised carbon crediting mechanism (successor to CDM under Kyoto)
Article 6.8: non-market approaches — cooperative implementation without trading
UPSC trap: Article 6 rulebook was NOT finalized at Paris (2015) — took until COP26 Glasgow (2021) to complete; COP29 further refined Article 6.4 standards

concepts.name: Transparency Framework: Enhanced Transparency Framework (ETF) vs. MRV under Kyoto
key_dimensions: Article 13: single Enhanced Transparency Framework (ETF) replacing the dual-track MRV system of Kyoto (which had different rules for developed/developing countries)
Biennial Transparency Reports (BTRs): all parties submit from 2024; replace Biennial Update Reports for developing countries
Built-in flexibility for developing countries lacking capacity — but NOT a different standard
UPSC trap: ETF has 'flexibility' for developing countries but is a SINGLE unified framework, unlike Kyoto's two-tier system

concepts.name: Paris Agreement's Entry into Force: Threshold, Ratification, and US Withdrawal/Re-entry
key_dimensions: Entry into force condition: 55 Parties representing 55% of global emissions — achieved on November 4, 2016
US withdrawal under Trump (effective November 4, 2020) and re-entry under Biden (February 19, 2021) — fastest possible timelines
Distinction between signing, ratifying, and entry into force — India ratified October 2, 2016 (Gandhi Jayanti)
UPSC trap: a Party can withdraw from Paris Agreement but NOT from the UNFCCC simultaneously without separate action

concepts.name: Adaptation vs. Mitigation in Paris Agreement: Global Goal on Adaptation (GGA)
key_dimensions: Article 7: Global Goal on Adaptation (GGA) — enhancing adaptive capacity, strengthening resilience, reducing vulnerability
GGA framework finalized at COP27; UAE Framework for Global Climate Resilience adopted at COP28
Unlike mitigation, adaptation is inherently local — no global metric like temperature for measurement
UPSC trap: developing countries (including India) pushed strongly for adaptation to have equal status with mitigation — Paris Agreement is the first to formally recognize a global adaptation goal

concepts.name: COP26 Glasgow Climate Pact: Key Outcomes and Relationship to Paris Agreement
key_dimensions: 'Phase down' (not 'phase out') of unabated coal — historic first mention of fossil fuels in a COP decision
Completion of Paris Rulebook (Article 6 carbon markets) after 6 years
Glasgow Climate Pact requested countries to revisit and strengthen 2030 NDCs by end of 2022
UPSC trap: the Glasgow Climate Pact is a COP Decision, NOT an amendment to the Paris Agreement; it has different legal standing

concepts.name: COP28 Dubai Outcomes: First Global Stocktake and 'Transitioning Away' from Fossil Fuels
key_dimensions: First GST finding: world is 'not on track' for 1.5°C; emissions need to fall 43% by 2030 vs. 2019 levels
UAE Consensus: call to 'transition away from fossil fuels' — first time all fossil fuels mentioned in a COP text
Tripling renewable energy capacity and doubling energy efficiency by 2030 — specific quantified targets
UPSC trap: 'transitioning away' is NOT the same as a phase-out commitment — language deliberately weakened from draft text

concepts.name: Relationship between Paris Agreement, UNFCCC, and Kyoto Protocol: Institutional Hierarchy
key_dimensions: Paris Agreement operates under the UNFCCC — CMA (Conference of Parties serving as Meeting of Parties to Paris Agreement) is its governing body
Kyoto Protocol's second commitment period (2013-2020) — Doha Amendment; Paris Agreement supersedes Kyoto for post-2020 period
UNFCCC Secretariat serves all three instruments; subsidiary bodies (SBSTA and SBI) serve all
UPSC trap: Paris Agreement did NOT replace or terminate the UNFCCC or Kyoto Protocol — all three remain in force simultaneously

concepts.name: Technology Mechanism and Capacity Building under Paris Agreement
key_dimensions: Technology Mechanism: Technology Executive Committee (TEC) + Climate Technology Centre and Network (CTCN) — established under UNFCCC, operationalized for Paris Agreement
Article 10: technology development and transfer — developed countries to provide support for developing countries
Paris Committee on Capacity-building (PCCB): established under Article 11 to address capacity gaps
UPSC trap: CTCN is the operational arm of the Technology Mechanism — hosted by UNEP in Copenhagen; often confused with Green Climate Fund

concepts.name: Green Climate Fund (GCF): Role, Governance, and Replenishment
key_dimensions: GCF is the primary dedicated financial mechanism of the UNFCCC/Paris Agreement — established at COP16 Cancun, operationalized at COP17 Durban
Headquartered in Incheon, South Korea — UPSC frequently tests the location
First replenishment (GCF-1): $9.8 billion (2019); Second replenishment (GCF-2): $9.3 billion pledged (2023)
UPSC trap: GCF is distinct from the Global Environment Facility (GEF) — GEF is older and serves multiple conventions; GCF is exclusively climate-focused

concepts.name: Emissions Gap and the Ambition Mechanism: NDC Insufficiency Problem
key_dimensions: UNEP Emissions Gap Report: annual assessment of gap between current NDC pledges and pathways needed for 1.5°C/2°C
Current NDCs (as of 2023-24) put world on track for approximately 2.5–2.9°C warming
The 'ambition gap' vs. the 'implementation gap' — two distinct problems in climate action
UPSC trap: submitting an NDC is binding; achieving it is NOT — countries face no legal penalty for missing NDC targets

concepts.name: Just Transition: Concept, COP Decisions, and Relevance for Developing Economies
key_dimensions: Just Transition Work Programme established at COP27 — ensures energy transition does not disproportionately harm workers and communities dependent on fossil fuels
Article 2(1)(b) of Paris Agreement: 'increasing the ability to adapt… in a manner that does not threaten food production' — foundational just transition language
India's position: right to development, historical emissions responsibility of developed countries, no premature phase-out
UPSC trap: 'Just Transition' appears in Paris Agreement preamble (for workforce) but the formal Work Programme was only created at COP27 — the Agreement itself does NOT mandate it as a program
